title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 35 (Finality of arbitral awards)

content.overview: Subject to Part I, an arbitral award shall be final and binding on the parties and persons claiming under them respectively.
content.glance: Subject to Part I, the arbitral award is final and binding on the parties and those claiming under them.
content.study: Section 35 confers finality and binding effect on the arbitral award, subject to the remedies and provisions of Part I. The award also binds persons claiming under the parties.

sections.heading: Final and binding
sections.body: Subject to Part I, the award is final and binding on the parties.

sections.heading: Persons claiming under the parties
sections.body: The award also binds persons claiming under them respectively.

sections.heading: Part I qualification
sections.body: Finality is subject to Part I remedies including correction, setting aside and appeal.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Is an arbitral award final under section 35?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Yes. Subject to Part I, an arbitral award shall be final and binding on the parties and persons claiming under them respectively.

examTips: Final and binding subject to Part I; extends to persons claiming under the parties.

enhancement.definition: Section 35 provides for finality of arbitral awards.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Subject to Part I, the award is final and binding on the parties and those claiming under them.
